source.title: Improving Training Stability for Multitask Ranking Models in Recommender Systems
source.authors: Jiaxi Tang; Yoel Drori; Daryl Chang; Maheswaran Sathiamoorthy; J. Gilmer; Li Wei; Xin-Yang Yi; Li-Chan Hong; Ed H. Chi

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, with supplementary sections. Some figure content is not numerically recoverable from the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: Reports experiments on how model size and complexity affect loss divergence, and evaluates clipping methods that mitigate training instability. The stability findings qualify broad claims about larger models and training recipes, but the study does not measure CIFAR classification error.
record.gate_note: Own results on model size, complexity, and instability bear on V1's model-size/training-stability theme, but the paper studies a YouTube multitask recommender and its loss-divergence/AUC/RMSE, not CIFAR training classification error or random labels. Rows below concern the study's measured training stability and recipes; they do not establish CIFAR training-error outcomes. Cited work in the related-work section is not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses the learning-rate–curvature stability account associated with V5 to motivate Clippy and evaluates training divergence and held-out performance. It does not measure the stability threshold, curvature dynamics, or recovery above that threshold. Its recommendation and translation experiments do not test V1's near-zero CIFAR training classification error or any other supplied version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors conclude that Clippy improves training stability over tested baselines in YouTube ranking models, with larger gains for more complex models and larger learning rates, while preserving convergence in those experiments. The translation supplement reports improvement over Adagrad but lower performance than AdamW. The authors leave theoretical justification and convergence guarantees to future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains multitask recommendation and translation models with Adagrad-based clipping methods and evaluates loss divergence and offline quality; it does not use the CIFAR classification-error recipes in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Training stability changes with model size and complexity, input-feature/task removals, learning rate, optimizer/clipping method, and warm-up schedule. Model-specific clipping effectiveness is also reported.

fits_no_version.finding: At 0.4x learning rate, untreated Large+DCN diverged in 5/5 runs; smaller size reduced this to 1/3, removing DCN, features, or one task to 2/3, and removing two tasks to 0/3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model size, complexity, features, and task sharing can affect divergence frequency in sequentially trained multitask recommendation models.

fits_no_version.finding: Clippy supported 2x learning rate across the three recommendation settings and improved held-out performance on Large+DCN; untreated training and some clipping settings diverged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Update clipping can improve training stability and held-out quality in these recommendation models.

fits_no_version.finding: Clippy had no divergent runs in the reported translation sweep and improved Adagrad's best validation error from 36.9% to 33.4%, while AdamW reached 31.6%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Clippy can increase Adagrad's learning-rate tolerance and improve translation validation performance in the tested setup.

record.problems: The evaluation protocol is indirect: stability is inferred from offline AUC/RMSE rather than a dedicated stability metric. Several conditions use only 3 or 5 runs; the authors say trial costs prevented more data points. The model is a simplified subset of the production recommender. Some learning-rate and layer-level results are figures without recoverable exact values.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for the six-task model's other four tasks: Section 5.2 says only two representative tasks are presented due to space limitations. Figure-only layer clipping factors and trajectories in Figures 4–8 are not assigned numeric rows where exact values are not stated. The cited prior-work results and experiments only mentioned as omitted or earlier trials are not extracted.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large CIFAR convolutional networks, including corrupted/random labels and the stated training-recipe qualifications.
Spurious local minima and the effect of one or two extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation with plain-network depth, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization, signal/gradient propagation, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization effects on training speed and depth.
Recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, accompanying curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence from measured below-threshold initial states.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V1 limits_scope verdict. Shared themes of model size and optimization instability do not establish a test of V1. References to curvature-based stability and recovered transient divergence also do not test V5 without the threshold-relative measurements it specifies. The corrected cannot_determine states concern the supplied versions, not uncertainty about the reported divergence counts.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, random or corrupted labels, random initialization, and SGD/Adam training to zero error are not measured; results use a YouTube multitask recommender and loss divergence/offline AUC or RMSE.

rows.subject: Large+DCN model, clean
rows.operation_detail: Measured full loss divergence across runs without training-stability treatments at 0.4x learning rate.
rows.note: The paper describes 5/5 runs as fully diverged when no change is applied.
rows.check: The 5/5 full-divergence result is correctly extracted, but it does not measure any supplied version's effect.

rows.subject: Small+DCN model
rows.operation_detail: Reduced model size relative to Large+DCN; measured loss divergence without stability treatments.
rows.note: The text says reducing model size yielded some surviving cases.
rows.check: The 1/3 divergence result measures recommendation-model stability, not near-zero training classification error or spurious local minima.

rows.subject: Large model
rows.operation_detail: Removed DCN-v2 layers relative to Large+DCN; measured loss divergence without stability treatments.
rows.note: The text says removing DCN-v2 layers yielded some surviving cases.
rows.check: The 2/3 divergence result is correctly extracted. Removing DCN layers does not isolate the depth and identity-shortcut comparison in V3.

rows.subject: Large+DCN model
rows.operation_detail: Removed a subset of input features; measured loss divergence without stability treatments.
rows.note: The authors state that removing input features can benefit stability.
rows.check: Feature-removal effects on divergence do not measure a supplied version.

rows.subject: Large+DCN model
rows.operation_detail: Removed one task; measured loss divergence without stability treatments.
rows.note: Table 3 reports the separate one-task removal condition.
rows.check: Task-removal effects on divergence do not measure a supplied version.

rows.subject: Large+DCN model
rows.operation_detail: Removed two tasks; measured loss divergence without stability treatments.
rows.note: Table 3 reports the separate two-task removal condition.
rows.check: Zero divergent runs out of three does not establish near-zero training error or another supplied effect.

rows.subject: Small
rows.operation_detail: Trained with no stability treatment (naive) and measured RMSE on the representative regression task.
rows.note: The paper says the naive method always suffers loss divergence, even on Small.
rows.check: Table 2 reports divergence rather than a numerical RMSE. This is a training-failure outcome, not evidence about V1.

rows.subject: Large
rows.operation_detail: Trained with no stability treatment (naive) and measured RMSE on the representative regression task.
rows.note: The paper says the naive method always suffers loss divergence.
rows.check: Table 2 reports divergence rather than a numerical RMSE. This is a training-failure outcome, not evidence about V1.

rows.subject: Large+DCN
rows.operation_detail: Trained with no stability treatment (naive) and measured RMSE on the representative regression task.
rows.note: The paper says the naive method always suffers loss divergence.
rows.check: Table 2 reports divergence rather than a numerical RMSE. This is a training-failure outcome, not evidence about V1.

rows.subject: Large+DCN
rows.operation_detail: Trained with layer-wise gradient clipping (GC); selected best learning rate and measured AUC and RMSE.
rows.note: GC can train this model at 1x, but the text says 2x leads to divergence.
rows.check: These are held-out AUC/RMSE results for a clipping baseline. The best learning rate is a selected setting, not a measured stability threshold.

rows.subject: Large+DCN
rows.operation_detail: Trained with adaptive gradient clipping (AGC); selected best learning rate and measured AUC and RMSE.
rows.note: AGC had very high variance at either 1x or 2x on Large+DCN; the table gives the selected 2x result.
rows.check: These are held-out AUC/RMSE results for a clipping baseline, not training classification error or threshold-relative recovery.

rows.subject: Large+DCN
rows.operation_detail: Trained with LAMB adapted to Adagrad; selected best learning rate and measured AUC and RMSE.
rows.note: Authors report LAMB trains without instability at 1x but convergence is negatively impacted.
rows.check: These are held-out performance results for an optimizer baseline. Its slower convergence does not test a supplied version.

rows.subject: Large+DCN
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Clippy; selected best learning rate and measured AUC and RMSE.
rows.note: Clippy handles all tabulated model settings at 2x; this compares an intervention that stabilizes training, not training classification error.
rows.check: This compares the study's own method with a baseline on held-out performance; it does not measure a supplied version.

rows.subject: Large+DCN
rows.operation_detail: Trained with GC at 2x learning rate; measured the evaluation metric trajectory.
rows.baseline: GC at 1x is the selected Table 2 condition
rows.note: The paper explicitly says GC on Large+DCN diverges at 2x.
rows.check: Divergence at 2x learning rate is stated, but 2x is relative to the original recipe, not a measured stability limit.

rows.subject: AdamW
rows.size_stated: six encoder and six decoder layers in the xformer_translate model
rows.operation_detail: Trained the translation model with AdamW; measured validation error and divergence.
rows.value: Diverged at learning rate 0.1 with 10k warm-up; best reported AdamW run: validation error rate 31.6% at learning rate 0.1 and 40k warm-up
rows.note: The selected best-run metric is reported separately from the divergence condition.
rows.check: The subject is the translation Transformer trained with AdamW, not AdamW as a model. Split divergence at 10k warm-up from the selected 31.6% validation-error result at 40k warm-up. Neither tests V1.

rows.subject: AdamW
rows.size_stated: six encoder and six decoder layers in the xformer_translate model
rows.operation_detail: Trained the translation model with AdamW; measured divergence.
rows.note: The text reports this distinct learning-rate and warm-up condition.
rows.check: The subject is the translation Transformer trained with AdamW. Divergence is reported without measuring its relation to a stability threshold.

rows.subject: Adagrad
rows.size_stated: six encoder and six decoder layers in the xformer_translate model
rows.operation_detail: Trained the translation model with Adagrad; measured divergence.
rows.note: The text says Adagrad diverged at learning rate 0.3 with either tested warm-up.
rows.check: The subject is the translation Transformer trained with Adagrad. The reported divergence at learning rate 0.3 applies to both 10k and 40k warm-up.

rows.subject: Adagrad
rows.size_stated: six encoder and six decoder layers in the xformer_translate model
rows.operation_detail: Trained the translation model with Adagrad; measured validation error and divergence.
rows.note: Reported as Adagrad's best run.
rows.check: The subject is the translation Transformer trained with Adagrad. This selected validation-error result is not training classification error.

rows.subject: Adagrad with Clippy
rows.size_stated: six encoder and six decoder layers in the xformer_translate model
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adagrad and Clippy; measured divergence across tested learning rates and validation error.
rows.baseline: AdamW and Adagrad have divergent runs at stated settings
rows.value: Did not diverge in any of the experiments
rows.note: Authors note that some earlier trials slowly diverged transitorily and later recovered.
rows.check: The subject is the translation Transformer trained with Adagrad and Clippy. The text describes two executions per learning rate, one for each warm-up duration, not two repetitions per learning-rate × warm-up condition. No divergence does not establish V5 without threshold and curvature measurements.

rows.subject: Adagrad with Clippy
rows.size_stated: six encoder and six decoder layers in the xformer_translate model
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adagrad and Clippy; measured validation error.
rows.baseline: Adagrad best run: 36.9% at learning rate 0.1 and 10k warm-up
rows.note: The text says this did not reach AdamW's performance but improved over Adagrad.
rows.check: The subject is the translation Transformer trained with Adagrad and Clippy. This selected validation-error comparison measures the proposed method's performance, not a supplied version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: YouTube multitask ranking models and the supplementary translation model
reader_labels.reason: Training stability varies with model size, complexity and clipping recipe; smaller models and some task/feature removals reduce divergence, while some large or faster-rate recipes still diverge (R1–R20). The study does not test the CIFAR training-error behavior named by V1.
